decision.title: Decision model
decision.description: Pick a decision model and where it applies. Off: every scenario takes its default path.
decision.remoteHint: The decision model can only be configured on this machine.
decision.offHint: The main model calls the browser tools and decides each step itself.
decision.jevHint: Jev decides each step in the browser and in desktop windows. Needs an API key.
decision.keySteps: → Sign up or log in → Create a new API key on the API Keys page.
decision.browserControlHint: Hands multi-step clicking and typing in the browser to the decision model.
decision.jevPrivacy: The task goal, on-screen content, control names and values, and the step history go to Jev (TypeSafe). Passwords are not read.
decision.computerControlHint: Hands multi-step work in desktop windows to the decision model.
decision.batchDecideHint: The main agent can hand bulk labelling, rating and yes/no judgement to the decision model. Item content is sent to Jev.
decision.smartApprovalHint: The decision model judges whether a call needs approval; privilege escalation, system files and credentials always ask. Off: built-in rules.
decision.memoryControlHint: Jev decides what to keep, how memories relate, and which ones to use before answering.

memory.title: Long-term memory
memory.defaultDesc: Always on. Local text search, with no model download.
memory.semanticDesc: A local multilingual model with full-text search; the first use downloads about 118 MB.
memory.jevDesc: Requires Jev selected, an API key saved, Enhanced memory checked, and the local model downloaded.
memory.jevNeedsDecision: First select Jev, save its API key, and check Enhanced memory in Decision engine.
memory.jevNeedsSystemTwo: First choose a System-Two large model in Memory settings.
memory.configureSemanticDesc: Enabled once the model download is confirmed.
memory.configureJevDesc: Enabled once the decision engine, System-Two model and local model are ready.
memory.decisionMissing: Configure the decision engine and check Enhanced memory
memory.downloadConfirm: Semantic memory needs a local model of about 118 MB. Download it now?
memory.jevDownloadConfirm: JEV memory needs the same local model, about 118 MB. Download it now?

memory.autoCaptureDesc: Stores your messages and the assistant's final reply, without tool output, reasoning or credentials.
memory.systemTwoModelDesc: Used when JEV needs to generalize; writes high-level summaries without changing the originals.

memory.graphDescription: Dots are memories, lines are relations, colour is the relation kind. Select a node for details.

remote.intro: Open the agent on this computer to other devices: a phone, a tablet, or a browser on another computer.
remote.setupDesc: Set a password that other devices log in with. It is kept only on this computer.
remote.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match
remote.enableDesc: Other devices can log in with the password and connect to the agent on this computer.
remote.lanAccessDesc: Devices on the same network can open the address below.
remote.lanAccessOnDesc: LAN address: {{address}}; the remote-access password is still required.
remote.lanAddressFamilyDesc: Choose whether LAN devices use the IPv4 or IPv6 address.
remote.tunnelHint: {{address}} is only this computer's local address. Pick a tunnel below to publish it.
remote.tunnelProviderDesc: The app starts it here and shows the public address below.
remote.tunnelIdle: The tunnel starts with the server once "Allow remote connections" above is on.
remote.tunnelScan: Scan or copy the address, then log in with the password set above. It changes every time the tunnel restarts.
remote.tunnelNeedsAuthDesc: {{name}} needs an authtoken from a free account. Run the command below with your own token, then press "Authenticated".
remote.tunnelSetupCloudflared: Cloudflare Tunnel is free and needs no account. Install cloudflared, then press "Installed".
remote.tunnelSetupNgrok: ngrok needs a free account: install it, then configure it once with your own authtoken.
remote.tunnelScanStable: Scan or copy the address, then log in with the password set above. It stays the same, so you can add it to your home screen.
remote.tunnelSetupFrp: frp needs a server of your own with a public address running frps, and frpc 0.52 or newer here.
remote.frpIntro: You need a server with a public IP running frps, and — for the HTTP domain mode — a domain that already resolves to that server. On a cloud server, its security group also has to allow frps's ports (the port below, plus the vhost or server port) — that is done in the provider's console. Fill in the details below and the app writes the frpc config and publishes remote access through your server.
remote.frpTokenPlaceholder: frps auth.token; leave empty if none
remote.frpTokenSaved: Saved; leave empty to keep it
remote.frpDomainHelp: HTTP mode finds this computer by domain, so add an A record pointing to the server's public IP{{target}}; frps also needs vhostHTTPPort (usually 80).
remote.frpNoDomain: No domain? Use TCP port mode and open the server IP and port on the phone.
remote.frpDnsMismatch: {{domain}} resolves to {{address}}, not the frps server ({{server}}). Point the A record at the server IP.
remote.frpDnsUnresolved: {{domain}} has no DNS record yet. Add an A record pointing to the frps server; it can take a few minutes to take effect.
remote.frpDnsResolved: {{domain}} resolves to {{address}} (the server address could not be resolved, so they were not compared).
remote.frpPublicUrlDesc: The address your phone opens. Empty derives it from the settings above; enter an https:// address when an HTTPS proxy fronts frps.
remote.frpInsecure: Unencrypted http: your password and conversations cross the network in plain text. Put an HTTPS proxy in front of frps.
